stem: According to kidney transplant infection references, which complication is described as the most common after kidney transplantation both early and late post-transplant?

options.text: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder as the leading early complication

explanation.rationale_correct: Genitourinary infection is cited as the most common complication after kidney transplantation in both early and late post-transplant periods, with incidence influenced by surgical and anatomic factors.

rationale_incorrect.B: Primary nonfunction is an early graft failure event, not the most common overall complication.
rationale_incorrect.C: Hyperacute rejection is rare compared with infectious complications.
rationale_incorrect.D: PTLD is a significant late complication but is not described as the most common early or overall complication.

stem: A kidney recipient on mycophenolate mofetil reports watery diarrhea three times daily without fever. According to transplant pharmacology references, what is the MOST appropriate initial teaching point?

options.text: GI adverse effects are common with MMF and may respond to transient dose reduction; persistent diarrhea despite MMF should not be ignored
Diarrhea on MMF always indicates acute rejection and requires immediate graft biopsy
Continue the same MMF dose indefinitely because GI symptoms never relate to drug toxicity
Stop all immunosuppression permanently at home without contacting the transplant team

explanation.rationale_correct: Diarrhea occurs in up to one-third of MMF recipients and often responds to transient dose reduction; persistent administration in the face of diarrhea is discouraged and can lead to inflammatory colitis.

rationale_incorrect.B: MMF-related diarrhea is a known adverse effect and does not always indicate rejection.
rationale_incorrect.C: GI symptoms are among the most common MMF adverse events and may require dose adjustment.
rationale_incorrect.D: Immunosuppression changes require transplant team guidance; permanent self-discontinuation risks rejection.

stem: A kidney recipient in the first month after transplant has repeated asymptomatic bacteriuria on screening cultures. According to post-transplant infection references, which outcome association should the coordinator emphasize when explaining why the team monitors this finding?

options.text: Frequent asymptomatic bacteriuria episodes are associated with pyelonephritis and development of acute rejection
Asymptomatic bacteriuria permanently prevents any future acute rejection
Bacteriuria in month one has no relationship to graft outcomes
Asymptomatic bacteriuria mandates immediate graft nephrectomy in all recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Early asymptomatic bacteriuria is common after kidney transplant, and frequent episodes are associated with pyelonephritis and development of acute rejection, supporting active monitoring and treatment decisions.

rationale_incorrect.B: Bacteriuria does not prevent rejection; it is associated with increased rejection risk when frequent.
rationale_incorrect.C: References link frequent bacteriuria to pyelonephritis and rejection, not a neutral finding.
rationale_incorrect.D: Nephrectomy is not the standard response to asymptomatic bacteriuria.

stem: A coordinator is teaching new staff about early post-kidney-transplant urinary complications. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Genitourinary infection is the most common complication after kidney transplantation.
Surgical complications such as urine leaks and lymphoceles can predispose to bacterial superinfection.
Genitourinary infection is rare in the immediate post-transplant period.
Female sex is among patient factors that predispose to post-transplant UTI.

explanation.rationale_correct: UTI is the most common kidney transplant complication, surgical issues such as leaks and lymphoceles predispose to superinfection, and female sex increases UTI risk. Statement III is false because early post-transplant UTI risk is substantial, not rare.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—female sex is listed among predisposing factors.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement III is false; early UTI risk is significant.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false; not all four statements are correct.
